item.text:
<linkedin_post>Website operators may soon have a simpler way to tell multiple AI providers how they want their content handled for foundational generative AI training.

OpenAI says it will honor a common signal in robots.txt, the file websites already use to communicate crawler preferences. Today, operators often need to maintain separate rules for each provider’s crawlers. A shared signal could reduce that work across providers that choose to honor it.

OpenAI aims to implement the signal in the coming months and says its existing crawler controls will continue to apply. The voluntary effort draws on work by the IETF AI Preferences working group, where discussions about a broader standard are ongoing.</linkedin_post>
